q-36585.name: Question 1
q-36585.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t)=q(t)
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(1+{t}^{2})+{x}_{2}(1-t+2{t}^{2}) & =1-3t+4{t}^{2} \\ ({x}_{1}+{x}_{2})-{x}_{2}t+({x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}){t}^{2} & =1-3t+4{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=1 \\ -{x}_{2}=-3 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=4.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 \\ 1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 \\ 1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=1 \\ -{x}_{2}=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=3.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}+(3)=1\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-2.
$$

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-2+3=1.$

q-106754.name: Question 2
q-106754.problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
{B}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}],\,{B}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 20 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

If $B=\{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}\},$ and $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$
q-106754.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{B}_{1}+{x}_{2}{B}_{2}=A.
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 20 & -2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 & 2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} & -2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 20 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=4 \\ 3{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=20 \\ -2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 4 \\ 3 & 4 & 20 \\ -2 & 3 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 4 \\ 3 & 4 & 20 \\ -2 & 3 & -2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-\frac{3}{2}){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 7 & 14 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=4 \\ 7{x}_{2}=14 \\ {x}_{2}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second and third equations, we get ${x}_{2}=2.$ From the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-2\cdot 2 & =4 \\ 2{x}_{1} & =8 \\ {x}_{1} & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=4+2=6.$

q-106761.name: Question 3
q-106761.problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
{B}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}],\,{B}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}9 & -18 \\ 15 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

If $B=\{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}\},$ and $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$
q-106761.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{B}_{1}+{x}_{2}{B}_{2}=A.
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}9 & -18 \\ 15 & 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} & -2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} & 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}9 & -18 \\ 15 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=9 \\ -2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-18 \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=15.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 9 \\ -2 & 2 & -18 \\ 3 & 1 & 15\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 9 \\ -2 & 2 & -18 \\ 3 & 1 & 15\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-\frac{3}{2}){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 9 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 \\ 0 & -\frac{1}{2} & \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=9 \\ 3{x}_{2}=-9 \\ -\frac{{x}_{2}}{2}=\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second and third equations, we get ${x}_{2}=-3.$ From the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} & =9 \\ 2{x}_{1}+(-3) & =9 \\ {x}_{1} & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -3\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=6+(-3)=3.$

q-106777.name: Question 4
q-106777.problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
{B}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,{B}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -8 \\ 7 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

If $B=\{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}\},$ and $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$
q-106777.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{B}_{1}+{x}_{2}{B}_{2}=A.
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -8 \\ 7 & 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} & -4{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} & 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -8 \\ 7 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-1 \\ -4{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=-8 \\ {x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=7.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & -2 & -8 \\ 1 & -2 & 7\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & -2 & -8 \\ 1 & -2 & 7\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 6 & -12 \\ 0 & -4 & 8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-1 \\ 6{x}_{2}=-12 \\ -4{x}_{2}=8.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second and third equations, we get ${x}_{2}=-2.$ From the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2\cdot (-2) & =-1 \\ {x}_{1} & =-1+4 \\ {x}_{1} & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=3+(-2)=1.$

q-106783.name: Question 5
q-106783.problem:
Consider the following polynomials:

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=1+t,\,{p}_{2}(t)=1-t+{t}^{2},\,q(t)=4+2{t}^{2}.
$$

If $B=\{{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)\},$ and $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$
q-106783.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t)=q(t)
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(1+t)+{x}_{2}(1-t+{t}^{2}) & =4+2{t}^{2} \\ ({x}_{1}+{x}_{2})+({x}_{1}-{x}_{2})t+{x}_{2}{t}^{2} & =4+2{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=4 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{2}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 4 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 4 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=4 \\ -2{x}_{2}=-4 \\ {x}_{2}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second and third  equations, we get ${x}_{2}=2.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}+(2)=4\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2.
$$

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=2+2=4.$
